newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania bars foreigners from bus company shares.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania bars foreigners from bus company shares.

text.p: Tanzania will bar foreigners from owning shares in the state-owned bus company when it goes on sale next year, a senior official at the Parastatal Sector Reform Commission said on Tuesday.

The sale aims to revive the UDA (Sharika la Usafari Dar es Salaam) which once controlled the capital's public transport but has been overtaken by privately-owned minibuses known as "daladalas", the official said.
Foreigners were prohibited from buying shares under the original terms of the commission's charter, the official added.

Divestiture of the state asset is scheduled for July, 1997 and under the terms of sale, 75 percent of UDA shares will be earmarked for indigenous investors while the government will retain a 25 percent stake, the official said.
The future of "daladalas" is uncertain because Tanzania wants a major revamp of the city's urban transport system.

Part of the transport sector reforms include new safety measures ordered by the government which on Monday reaffirmed an order that all public buses be fitted with speed governors by the end of the month.

Local media quoted home affairs minisiter Ali Mohamed as saying the devices were necessary in order to prevent reckless driving and reduce road accidents which have claimed 5,500 lives in the past three and a half years.
At a foreign investment and technology forum earlier this month, the privatisation commission said it had approved the sale of 138 parastatals by June 30 worth $78.2 million.
